test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 28 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Who was NOT a member of the Cabinet Mission?
solution:
The correct answer is** __Sir John Simon.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__****

__
 
• **John Allsebrook Simon, 1st Viscount Simon**, was a British politician who held senior Cabinet posts from the beginning of the First World War to the end of the Second World War.
 
• The Indian Statutory Commission, commonly referred to as the Simon Commission after its chairman **Sir John Allsebrook Simon**, was sent to India in 1928.
 
• The British government constituted a Statutory Commission **under Sir John Simon**.
 
• The commission was made to look into the functioning of the constitutional system in India and suggest changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Albert Victor Alexander, 1st Earl Alexander of Hillsborough** was a British Labour and Co-operative politician. He was three times First Lord of the Admiralty, including during the Second World War, and then Minister of Defence under Clement Attlee.
 
• **Frederick William Pethick-Lawrence**, 1st Baron Pethick-Lawrence, PC was a British Labour politician who, among other things, campaigned for women's suffrage from 1945 to 1947 he was Secretary of State for India and Burma and was involved in the negotiations that led to India's independence in 1947. Prime Minister Clement Attlee, however, made all the government's major decisions regarding India
 
• **S****ir Richard Stafford Cripps **was a British Labour Party politician, barrister, and diplomat. A wealthy lawyer by background, he first entered Parliament at a by-election in 1931.
